title: Matt Damon's Ship From 'The Odyssey' Needs Your Help
summary:
The lifesize wooden ship in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey needs some care, and its owners are looking for volunteers to help. The 50-oar Draken Harald Hårfagre is due for routine maintenance, and volunteers can apply online, if they can get to Norway by April 2027.

'A project like Draken depends not only on a professional crew and sailing deckhands, but also on dedicated volunteers who help support the life of the ship,' its official website says. Volunteering is a hands-on way to help while learning about the ship.

Nolan's movie version of The Odyssey is huge, and much of its scale comes from real effects instead of computer images. The director used full-sized set pieces like a real Trojan Horse. For Odysseus' galley ship, Nolan used the Draken. The ship is not exactly right for the time of The Odyssey, but neither is the movie's modern English dialogue, or Matt Damon as Odysseus.

The Draken was ordered in 2010 by Norwegian businessman Sigurd Aase. It is built with overlapping oak planks, based on ship descriptions in Viking poems. At 114 feet long and 26 feet wide, with a single 79-foot-tall mast, it is a bigger version of the famous Gokstad ship, built around 890 CE. Its first voyage was in 2012, and in 2016 a crew of 100 rowers recreated the Vikings' crossing from Norway to Newfoundland.
why_it_matters: It shows kids that real history and movie magic can meet, and that volunteers can help keep a piece of the past alive.
